3.3 Black-Box Test Design

Specification-based (black-box) testing focuses on testing the functionality of software components against specified business rules and database schemas without relying on internal code implementation details.

3.3.1 Equivalence Partitioning (EP)

Equivalence Partitioning divides the input domain into discrete equivalence classes where all data values within a class are treated equivalently by the system. One representative value is chosen from each class to eliminate redundant execution while guaranteeing functional coverage.

Table 3.3.1: EP Specification for Student Registration (POST /api/auth/register)

3.3.2 Boundary Value Analysis (BVA)

Boundary Value Analysis focuses testing on the boundaries of equivalence partitions. Software exhibits the highest defect density at boundary edges due to off-by-one errors and date/time edge cases. BVA tests the 6 critical points: min-1, min, min+1, max-1, max, max+1.

Table 3.3.4: BVA on Numeric, Temporal, and Date Variables

Variable Nominal Rule Test Value Boundary Point Expected Response Actual Response Status

Slot Duration Lower limit: 5 min 5 min (09:00-09:05) min Accept (HTTP 201); valid minimum Accepted (HTTP 201) Pass
Slot Duration Lower limit: 5 min 6 min (09:00-09:06) min + 1 Accept (HTTP 201); valid slot Accepted (HTTP 201) Pass
Slot Duration Upper limit: 480 min 479 min (08:00-15:59) max - 1 Accept (HTTP 201); valid slot Accepted (HTTP 201) Pass

Slot Duration Upper limit: 480 min 481 min (08:00-16:01) max + 1 Reject (HTTP 400); duration > 480 Rejected (HTTP 400) Pass* (BUG-07)
Password Length Min length: 6 chars 5 chars ("Ab@12") min - 1 Reject (HTTP 400); length < 6 Rejected (HTTP 400) Pass
Password Length Min length: 6 chars 6 chars ("Abc@12") min Accept (HTTP 201); valid boundary Accepted (HTTP 201) Pass
Password Length Min length: 6 chars 7 chars ("Abcd@12") min + 1 Accept (HTTP 201); valid password Accepted (HTTP 201) Pass
Cancellation Deadline Deadline: 2 hours (120m) 119m before start Deadline - 1 min Reject cancellation (HTTP 400) Rejected (HTTP 400) Pass

Defect Discovery & Root Cause Analysis

BUG-01 (GitHub Issue #2): Impossible Month Acceptance (2027-13-01)
The model regex /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ validates string shape but not semantic month range. V8 new Date("2027-13-01...") returns Invalid Date, whose .getTime() is NaN. Because NaN ≤ Date.now() is false in IEEE-754 arithmetic, the system erroneously assumes the date is in the future and accepts it into MongoDB.
BUG-02 (GitHub Issue #3): Calendar Rollover on Non-Existent Date (2027-02-31)
The V8 Date constructor silently rolls 3 excess days over into March 3. However, MongoDB stores the raw string "2027-02-31". Subsequent queries on March 3 fail string matching, creating unqueryable orphaned records.
BUG-07 (GitHub Issue #9): Missing Upper Boundary Information in Error Message
Testing 481 minutes returned: "End time must be after start time, and slot duration must be at least 5 minutes", failing to state that the 480-minute maximum boundary was exceeded.
BUG-08 (GitHub Issue #15): Misleading Duration Error in updateAvailability
Discovered and logged by Member 2 (Yasiru-Nawodya): When updating a slot with a duration < 5 minutes, the backend returns: "End time must be after start time", even when end time is chronologically after start time (e.g. 10:00 to 10:04).
Figure 3.3.9: GitHub Issue #15 logged by Yasiru-Nawodya in team repository smart-lecture-appointment-management-system-QA.

3.3.3 Decision Table Testing: Appointment Booking (POST /api/appointments)

Decision Table testing specifies and verifies complex business logic governed by combinations of multiple conditions. In bookAppointment, 7 conditions govern 8 system actions.

The unconstrained domain of 7 conditions contains 27 = 128 combinations. Applying condition collapse based on short-circuit early-exit guards reduces the 128 combinations down to 8 logically independent, fully executable rules (R1 to R8).

3.4 White-Box Testing (LO-2)

White-box (structural) testing verifies internal control paths, branch coverage, statement coverage, and cyclomatic complexity.

3.4.1 Control Flow Graph (CFG) Construction

The primary target function is createAvailability in backend/controllers/availabilityController.js. The controller is partitioned into 14 nodes (13 basic blocks + terminal Exit node) and 18 directed control edges (13 internal transitions + 5 exit connections to terminal Exit).

Figure 3.4.1: Control Flow Graph for createAvailability showing 14 nodes (13 basic blocks + terminal Exit node), 18 directed edges (13 internal + 5 to Exit), and 5 decision nodes.

3.4.2 Cyclomatic Complexity Calculation ($V(G)=6$)

Cyclomatic Complexity $V(G)$ is calculated and proven using three independent mathematical formulas:

Method 1 (Edge-Node Formula):
V(G) = E - N + 2P = 18 - 14 + 2(1) = 4 + 2 = 6
Method 2 (Predicate Formula):
V(G) = Pdecision + 1 = 5 + 1 = 6
(Decision Nodes: Node 2, Node 4, Node 6, Node 9, Node 10)
Method 3 (Planar Regions Formula):
V(G) = R = Enclosed Regions + Exterior Region = 5 + 1 = 6

3.4.3 Linearly Independent Basis Paths

Because $V(G) = 6$, there are exactly 6 linearly independent basis paths:

Table 3.4.1: Independent Basis Paths for createAvailability

Path ID Node Sequence Traversal Description Concrete Test Input Expected Result
Path 1 1 → 2 → 3 Decision 1 = True (Missing fields) { date: "...", startTime: "...", endTime: "...", location: "" } HTTP 400 Bad Request
Path 2 1 → 2 → 4 → 5 Decision 2 = True (Duration < 5 min) { startTime: "10:00", endTime: "10:04" } (4 min) HTTP 400 Bad Request
Path 3 1 → 2 → 4 → 6 → 7 Decision 3 = True (Past date) { date: "2020-01-01", startTime: "10:00" } HTTP 400 Bad Request
Path 4 1 → 2 → 4 → 6 → 8 → 9 → 10 → 11 Decision 4 = True, 5 = True (Slot overlap) Existing: 10-11, New: 10:30-11:30 HTTP 400 Bad Request
Path 5 1 → 2 → 4 → 6 → 8 → 9 → 10 → 9 → 12 → 13 Existing slots checked; no overlap; slot created Existing: 08-09, New: 10:00-11:00 HTTP 201 Created
Path 6 1 → 2 → 4 → 6 → 8 → 9(empty) → 12 → 13 Zero existing slots; loop bypassed; slot created 0 existing slots on 2026-12-25; New: 10:00-11:00 HTTP 201 Created

3.4.4 Statement vs. Branch Coverage Analysis

Key Finding: Statement coverage requires a minimum of 5 test cases (Paths 1 to 5). In contrast, Branch coverage strictly requires all 6 Basis Paths because exercising the False outcome of Decision Node 9 (loop executed zero times when no existing slots exist) requires Path 6.
Figure 3.4.2: Jest coverage report verifying 100% statement, branch, and line coverage on dateUtils.js and 71.62% overall backend branch coverage.

3.4.5 Supplementary White-Box Analysis (isValidTimeRange)

In backend/utils/dateUtils.js, isValidTimeRange contains a compound predicate composed of 3 relational checks (end > start, duration ≥ 5, duration ≤ 480). Decomposing this predicate yields $V(G) = 3 + 1 = 4$.

Figure 3.4.3: Supplementary Control Flow Graph for isValidTimeRange showing compound condition decomposition.

3.10 Member 2 Individual QA Self-Reflection

Student Name: Yasiru Nawodya • GitHub Account: Yasiru-Nawodya

Assigned Role: Member 2 â€“ Black-Box & White-Box Test Design (LO-2)

Feature Branch: member2-test-design • Pull Request: #14 (Passed CI & SonarCloud)

1. Scope of Work & Major Achievements

Under Learning Outcome 2, I authored the complete black-box test design (EP, BVA, Decision Tables) and white-box structural testing specifications. I designed 13 distinct test partitions, 21 BVA test points, an 8-rule collapsed decision table, constructed formal CFG diagrams, mathematically derived Cyclomatic Complexity $V(G)=6$, and proved the fundamental difference between statement and branch coverage.

2. Technical Lessons Learned

  • Flaws of Syntactic Validation: Regular expressions like /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ validate format shape but fail completely on calendar semantics, leading to critical bugs like month 13 (BUG-01) and February 31 rollover (BUG-02).
  • Branch Coverage Subsumes Statement Coverage: Proving that 5 tests achieve 100% statement coverage while 6 tests are strictly required for 100% branch coverage demonstrated the practical importance of basis path testing in enterprise QA.
  • Defect Prevention: Applying condition collapse to the booking decision table eliminated race conditions and double-booking vulnerabilities before code changes were merged.

3. Git Workflow & Collaborative Synergies

All work was developed strictly within member2-test-design across 9 modular, authentic commits without pushing directly to main. PR #14 was opened with passing SonarCloud Quality Gate and Jest backend test suites.
